overlapping_phenotypes: axial hypotonia progressing to spastic tetraparesis, cerebellar atrophy, optic atrophy, corpus callosum thinning
discriminating_logic: Presence of sparse/slow-growing hair/alopecia supports JABELS over INAD (where hair is normal). Brain iron accumulation is absent in infant JABELS but present early in INAD.

overlapping_phenotypes: progressive lower limb spasticity, hyperreflexia, motor delay
discriminating_phenotype: early central hypotonia, microcephaly, epilepsy, choreoathetosis, ectodermal involvement
discriminating_logic: Presence of microcephaly, epilepsy, choreoathetosis, severe cognitive impairment, and ectodermal involvement rules out uncomplicated HSPs.

overlapping_phenotypes: severe microcephaly, severe global developmental delay, marked infratentorial volume loss
discriminating_phenotype: progressive cerebellar hemisphere and vermian atrophy with preserved pontine bulk, sparse hair
discriminating_logic: Preserved pontine bulk with progressive cerebellar atrophy and sparse scalp hair distinguishes JABELS from PCH's congenital pontine flattening.

overlapping_phenotypes: hypotonia, cerebellar ataxia, developmental delay, vermian hypoplasia
discriminating_phenotype: molar tooth sign absence, prominent hypotrichosis, absence of ciliary hallmarks
discriminating_logic: Absence of true molar tooth sign on neuroradiological review and absence of ciliary hallmarks (cystic renal disease, polydactyly) accompanied by hypotrichosis distinguishes JABELS from Joubert syndrome.
